categories.label: Life Sciences & Healthcare
categories.definition: Resources whose principal subject is biology, medicine, health, clinical care, biomedical research, or pharmaceuticals.
categories.scopeNote: Use for biological and biomedical subject matter, anatomy, disease, clinical practice, health services, and related life-science data. Prefer Environment & Agriculture when environmental or farming concerns are primary.

categories.label: Geospatial
categories.definition: Resources centered on geographic location, spatial relationships, mapping, geodesy, or Earth observation.
categories.scopeNote: Use for GIS, cartography, cadastral data, place identifiers, coordinate systems, and explicitly spatial datasets. Do not use solely because a domain can contain locations.

categories.label: Government & Public Sector
categories.definition: Resources for government, law, public administration, public services, civic institutions, or defense.
categories.scopeNote: Use when national, regional, or local public-sector operations and legal or civic information are primary. Prefer International Development for aid, humanitarian, and cross-country development programs.

categories.label: International Development
categories.definition: Resources for international aid, humanitarian action, sustainable development, and cross-country social or economic development.
categories.scopeNote: Use for development programs, global development indicators, humanitarian response, and aid organizations. Prefer Government & Public Sector for domestic administration and public services.

categories.label: Finance & Business
categories.definition: Resources for finance, accounting, markets, commerce, enterprise operations, industry, or business transactions.
categories.scopeNote: Use for financial instruments and institutions, corporate information, products and services, supply chains, and commercial processes.

categories.label: Library & Cultural Heritage
categories.definition: Resources for libraries, archives, museums, bibliography, language, the arts, history, or cultural heritage collections.
categories.scopeNote: Use for cataloging and authority data, archival description, museum collections, historical and artistic subjects, linguistic vocabularies, and cultural memory.

categories.label: Technology & Web
categories.definition: Resources whose principal subject is computing, data technology, telecommunications, the internet, or web standards.
categories.scopeNote: Use for domain-specific computing and web concepts. Prefer General / Cross-domain for foundational semantic models designed to apply across subject domains.

categories.label: Environment & Agriculture
categories.definition: Resources for the environment, climate, ecology, natural resources, agriculture, forestry, food production, or fisheries.
categories.scopeNote: Use when environmental systems, conservation, land and water management, farming, crops, livestock, or food production are primary.

categories.label: General / Cross-domain
categories.definition: Foundational, upper-level, broadly reusable, or genuinely multi-domain resources without one dominant subject domain.
categories.scopeNote: Use as the fallback when no more specific category is supported, and for general metadata, modeling, and cross-domain conceptual resources.

softwareTypes.label: Graph Database
softwareTypes.definition: A storage engine for persisting and querying graph-structured data, including RDF triplestores, quadstores, and property-graph databases.
softwareTypes.scopeNote: Use when durable graph storage and query are primary. Exclude clients, visualization tools, mapping systems, and general libraries that merely connect to a graph database.

softwareTypes.label: SPARQL Tooling
softwareTypes.definition: Software whose primary purpose is running, constructing, managing, federating, or optimizing SPARQL queries.
softwareTypes.scopeNote: Use for SPARQL clients, GUIs, query builders, and federation or optimization engines. Exclude the data store itself.

softwareTypes.label: Ontology Engineering
softwareTypes.definition: Software for authoring, editing, validating, documenting, publishing, or aligning ontologies and controlled vocabularies.
softwareTypes.scopeNote: Use for editors, modeling environments, pitfall scanners, documentation generators, and alignment tools. Exclude standalone reasoning engines.

softwareTypes.label: Reasoning & Inference
softwareTypes.definition: Software that performs logical inference, entailment, consistency checking, or classification over RDF, RDFS, or OWL knowledge.
softwareTypes.scopeNote: Use when reasoning is the primary function. Exclude editors and general libraries that only invoke a separate reasoner.

softwareTypes.label: RDF Data Mapping / ETL
softwareTypes.definition: Software that converts non-RDF data into RDF or virtualizes non-RDF sources as RDF.
softwareTypes.scopeNote: Use for relational, spreadsheet, CSV, XML, or other source-to-RDF conversion, including R2RML and ontology-based data access systems.

softwareTypes.label: Developer Library
softwareTypes.definition: A programming-language library or SDK for developers building software that works with RDF, OWL, or graph data-model constructs.
softwareTypes.scopeNote: Use for reusable code libraries rather than end-user applications. Prefer a more specific type when storage, reasoning, mapping, or another function is the product's primary purpose.

softwareTypes.label: Knowledge Graph Construction
softwareTypes.definition: Software that constructs a knowledge graph as a deliverable dataset from schemas, structured sources, or unstructured content.
softwareTypes.scopeNote: Use when producing an exportable or independently consumable graph is the point, including systems that use AI internally. Exclude graphs used only as an agent's runtime memory.

softwareTypes.label: AI Agent Tooling
softwareTypes.definition: Software in which graph structures primarily support an AI agent's runtime memory, grounding, context, or execution interface.
softwareTypes.scopeNote: Use when the graph serves the agent's operation. Prefer Knowledge Graph Construction when the primary output is a standalone graph dataset.

softwareTypes.label: Visualization
softwareTypes.definition: Software for visually rendering or interactively exploring ontologies, graphs, or semantic query results.
softwareTypes.scopeNote: Use when visual presentation and exploration are primary, rather than incidental displays within an editor, database, or query client.

softwareTypes.label: Stream Processing
softwareTypes.definition: Software for processing RDF or graph data as continuous streams rather than as static or batch datasets.
softwareTypes.scopeNote: Use for RDF stream processing and continuous semantic queries. Exclude conventional databases that support only stored-data queries.
